facts.statement: Shantungosaurus is the largest known hadrosauroid taxon, with estimated lengths of 15 to 17 meters and body masses of 13 to 16 metric tons.
facts.quote: Shantungosaurus is so far the largest hadrosauroid taxon in the world, with size estimates around 15 - 17 m in length and 13 - 16 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Shantungosaurus had a toothless beak but possessed approximately 1,500 tiny teeth in its jaws for chewing.
facts.quote: Like all hadrosaurs its beak was toothless, but its jaws were packed with around 1,500 tiny chewing teeth.

facts.statement: A large hole near the nostrils may have been covered by a loose flap of skin that could be inflated to produce sounds.
facts.quote: Un gran hueco cerca de los orificios de la nariz pudo haber estado cubierto de una solapa de tejido que pudo inflarla para producir sonidos.

facts.statement: Shantungosaurus was first described in 1973 and is known from more than five incomplete skeletons unearthed between 1964 and 1968.
facts.quote: First described in 1973, Shantungosaurus is known from over five incomplete skeletons that were unearthed from 1964 to 1968.

facts.statement: The genus was discovered in 1964 and is known from five incomplete skeletons found in the Wangshi Formation of Shandong Province, China.
facts.quote: Descubierto en 1964, este género es conocido por 5 esqueletos incompletos encontrados en la Formación Wangshi de la provincia de Shandong, China.

facts.statement: Shantungosaurus lived during the middle to late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The stratigraphic interval of Shantungosaurus ranges from the top of the Xingezhuang Formation to the middle of the Hongtuya Formation, middle to late Campanian in age.

facts.statement: Shantungosaurus lived approximately 77 to 70 million years ago during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 77 a 70 millones de años durante el campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Shantungosaurus was a heavy quadruped with massive legs to support its bulky body.
facts.quote: Era un dinosaurio pesado, con cuatro patas macizas para soportar su voluminoso cuerpo.

facts.statement: Shantungosaurus could walk on its hind legs equipped with hooves, but also on all four legs since its hands ended in hooves as well.
facts.quote: Podía avanzar sobre las patas traseras provistas de cascos, pero también sobre las cuatro patas, ya que sus manos estaban terminadas también en cascos.

facts.statement: Shantungosaurus used its beak to gather large amounts of tough plants in one bite and crushed them into a paste using around 1,500 tiny cheek teeth.
facts.quote: con el que recogía grandes cantidades de plantas duras de un solo bocado y las trituraba hasta convertirlas en una pasta, sirviéndose de alrededor de 1500 diminutos dientes de sus carrillos.

facts.statement: Specimens originally classified as Zhuchengosaurus maximus in 2007 were later determined to be Shantungosaurus, with differences attributed to growth stages.
facts.quote: Remains of several individuals, including skull bones, limb bones, and vertebrae, were found in Shandong, China. These specimens were classified in the new genus and species Zhuchengosaurus maximus in 2007. However, further study showed that the supposedly distinct features of Zhuchengosaurus were simply a result of different growth stages.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2016 that Shantungosaurus size estimates should be moderated to 15 meters and 13 metric tons, though it remains the largest hadrosaur.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul suggested that previous studies have overestimated the size of this dinosaur, moderating it at 15 m in length and 13 MT in body mass, which still makes this dinosaur the largest hadrosaur.

rejected.statement: Analyses interpret Zhuchengosaurus and Huaxiaosaurus, known from the same region, as junior synonyms of Shantungosaurus.
rejected.quote: Zhuchengosaurus y Huaxiaosaurus, ambos conocidos de la misma región, han sido interpretados por los análisis como sinónimos más modernos de Shantungosaurus.

rejected.quote: There are possible records from the Maastrichtian, although these are uncertain.
